findings.source: exit code 0 is defined as 'audit completed and no HIGH finding'
findings.sink: AGENT-RUNTIME-CONFIG-INCOMPLETE-001 is MEDIUM (plan:118), and exit 3 is only 'audit could not complete' (plan:155-156)
findings.missing_check: no mapping from incomplete coverage to a non-zero exit; 0 is reachable with an unparsed recognized surface
findings.evidence: design/agent-guard-plan.md:152 "0: audit completed and no HIGH finding"; :118 AGENT-RUNTIME-CONFIG-INCOMPLETE-001 is MEDIUM; :155-156 exit 3 is only "audit could not complete"; plan:286-287 test 3 demands "incomplete coverage, not a pass" the exit table cannot express. Alternative reading of the :155-156 parenthetical tried and rejected: the table is explicit and nothing maps a MEDIUM coverage finding to non-zero.

findings.source: rule table has no hook-command or MCP-stdio-command rule; policy says it evaluates config facts, not command strings (plan:248-250)
findings.sink: hooks execute automatically and MCP stdio commands run at startup without a model tool call; existing instruction_guard already flags hooks (instruction_guard.py:3621-3643, 3798-3816) and analyzes Cursor MCP commands (4156-4190)
findings.missing_check: execution authority is not derived from presence of hook commands or MCP command fields
findings.evidence: design/agent-guard-plan.md:110-119 rule table has no hook/MCP-command rule; :248-250 "evaluates configuration facts, not actual command strings" excludes the executing fields; instruction_guard.py:3798-3822 IG-ACTIVE-DANGEROUS-HOOK HIGH and :4156-4190 Cursor MCP command/args (sh -c at :4182-4184) already treat this evidence as in scope, so a clean agent-audit would contradict an existing in-tree HIGH.

findings.source: discovery lists user and project config layers without precedence
findings.sink: a project settings.local.json or project MCP manifest can grant what the user config denies
findings.missing_check: no per-agent layer order, merge rule, or unknown-precedence coverage state
findings.evidence: design/agent-guard-plan.md:226-231 lists user and project layers with no merge/precedence rule; instruction_guard.py:4088 itself records "effective permissions depend on Cursor mode and higher-priority policy" and that repository-controlled settings cross a project trust boundary. Exact vendor precedence unverified (see not_verified); the absent model is verified.

findings.source: secret classes are .env*, SSH, cloud credential files, AuraScan .env and 'another recognized secret store'
findings.sink: same-UID shell can read environment variables, agent auth stores, VCS/package credentials, sockets and absolute paths outside --root
findings.missing_check: no env/socket/auth-store/VCS-credential classes; reachability scoped to cwd/home rather than UID-readable
findings.evidence: design/agent-guard-plan.md:116/:244-246 class list omits env vars, agent auth stores, VCS/package credentials and sockets; agent.py:138-148 AGENT_SENSITIVE_PATH_RE is broader (histories, rc files, /proc/self/environ at :142) and agent.py:1943-1960 minimal_agent_environment shows the repo treats inherited env as an authority channel.

findings.source: egress is 'unrestricted' or ambiguous, and policy includes sandbox/egress claims and approval modes (plan:246)
findings.sink: config claims and an approval prompt are not OS boundaries; a shell on a normal host has network by default
findings.missing_check: no host-relative isolation fact; config claims are treated as proof and ambiguity as a HIGH detection
findings.evidence: design/agent-guard-plan.md:117 asserts HIGH "unrestricted" from ambiguity and :246 evaluates "sandbox/egress claims" — config claims are not enforcement points; article-notes.md:21-24 records the allowlist lesson. Ambiguity-as-detection is the verified core; the host-relative prescription is design judgment on top.

findings.source: .env* matches .env.example/.template/sample; ~/.ssh, keyrings and browser stores are ubiquitous
findings.sink: aggregate rule 119 fires on an ordinary developer machine with a shell tool
findings.missing_check: no separation between inventory (MEDIUM/INFO) and capability (HIGH); no example/template exclusion
findings.evidence: design/agent-guard-plan.md:116 ".env*" glob covers .env.example/.template/.sample by shelling-glob semantics; plan:269-270 admits the same-UID reality, so rule 119's aggregate (plan:119) fires whenever a shell tool and any matched class coexist. Prevalence on real machines is [Inference, Red-acknowledged]; the calibration defect (no template exclusion, no inventory-vs-capability split) is verified.

findings.source: remote model reference is checked as a URL and trust state, not fetched; report digest only
findings.sink: config files and the model endpoint can change after the audit; no captured_at or input digest
findings.missing_check: no per-input digest (path/dev/ino/size/mtime/sha256), no freshness field, no revalidate-before-run requirement
findings.evidence: design/agent-guard-plan.md:271-273 digests the report only; no per-input digest, captured_at or freshness field exists anywhere in the plan (full-text read); article-notes.md:19-20 records the operator-swappable payload, so snapshot staleness is a real channel.

findings.source: model is UNVERIFIED unless a local trust entry exists
findings.sink: a user-created trust entry suppresses the provenance finding; a pinned hash proves identity at audit time, not safety
findings.missing_check: trust entry is treated as verification and is allowed to remove the finding
findings.evidence: design/agent-guard-plan.md:114 makes the finding disappear on "a locally approved trust entry" — a user action, not verification; the rule name invites "no finding = model verified". Verified as plan text; operator swap behavior is [Inference].

findings.source: parsers are bounded but discovery traversal has no entry/depth/time bounds
findings.sink: the existing guard resolve_regular_file rejects directories (guards.py:43-77); a new walker is required
findings.missing_check: no bounded directory walker (entries/depth/time/prune) and no explicit coverage on truncation
findings.evidence: design/agent-guard-plan.md:233-236 bounds parsers only; mcp/guards.py:43-79 resolve_regular_file is regular-file-only (rejects directory/FIFO/socket/device at :75-76); no walker primitive exists in-tree.

findings.source: report digest is computed by the same unprivileged code and the desktop refuses a changed report
findings.sink: a same-UID writer can rewrite the report and recompute the digest
findings.missing_check: no distinction between corruption detection and tamper protection; no key outside the UID's reach
findings.evidence: design/agent-guard-plan.md:271-273 "Report integrity ... must refuse a changed report" immediately after :269-270 admits same-UID readers; the digest is computed by the same unprivileged code, so it is a consistency check, not tamper protection.

findings.source: --model accepts a local directory/file or HTTP(S) endpoint; report redacts raw model paths
findings.sink: local directory hashing is unbounded; URL userinfo/query/fragment is not specified for redaction
findings.missing_check: no byte cap for model metadata, no URL userinfo rejection or query/fragment stripping
findings.evidence: design/agent-guard-plan.md:96 accepts PATH_OR_URL with no byte-cap rule for local hashing and no URL userinfo/query/fragment redaction (:252-257 covers raw paths only); AGENTS.md requires userinfo/query/fragment redaction in persisted acquisition metadata.

findings.sink: no test for incomplete-surface exit code, defaults, precedence, hooks/MCP commands, env secrets, large/rooted trees, MCP oracle, terminal injection, 'no HIGH != safe' wording, post-audit config change, or model URL components
findings.missing_check: the test plan does not falsify the load-bearing claims
findings.evidence: design/agent-guard-plan.md:277-302: the ten tests omit incomplete-surface exit codes, defaults/precedence, hook/MCP-command exec, env secrets, bounded trees, MCP oracle, terminal injection, post-audit change and URL components; the plan's core claims are unfalsified by its own test list.

findings.source: plan says instruction_guard does not inspect an agent's shell/exec configuration and that the audit reduces reachability
findings.sink: instruction_guard.py:1577-1612 classifies settings/manifests, 3621-3643/3798-3816 flags hooks, 4156-4190 analyzes MCP commands, 2533-2540 flags project shell enablement
findings.missing_check: the plan does not state the relationship to existing Instruction Guard coverage; 'reduces reachability' is not what an audit does
findings.evidence: design/agent-guard-plan.md:38-42 "[Instruction Guard] does not inspect ... an agent's shell/exec configuration" is false for classification/hook/MCP parts (instruction_guard.py:1577-1613, :3621-3643, :4156-4190); plan:269-270 "The audit reduces reachability" is wrong — an audit reports, only remediation or a sandbox reduces.
